problem:
Consider the solution curves of the differential equation ${y}^{′}-y={x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}.$ Which of the following are stationary points of their respective solution curve?

- $(-1,-2)$
- $(1,1)$
- $(1,-2)$

feedback.problem:
Consider the solution curves of the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2y-4x}{x}.
$$

 

Which of the following are stationary points of their respective solution curve?

- $(1,5)$
- $(-2,-4)$
- $(-1,-3)$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that a stationary point of $f(x)$ is a point $x=c$ in the domain of $f$ such that ${f}^{′}(c)=0.$ 

With that in mind, let's examine each of the given points. We substitute the coordinates of our points into the differential equation and calculate the value of the derivative: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(1,5)} & ={(\frac{2y-4x}{x})|}_{(1,5)} \\  & =\frac{2(5)-4(1)}{1} \\  & =6 \\  & \ne 0\,\times  \\ {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(-2,-4)} & ={(\frac{2y-4x}{x})|}_{(-2,-4)} \\  & =\frac{2(-4)-4(-2)}{(-2)} \\  & =0\,✓ \\ {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(-1,-3)} & ={(\frac{2y-4x}{x})|}_{(-1,-3)} \\  & =\frac{2(-3)-4(-1)}{(-1)} \\  & =2 \\  & \ne 0\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."
